h1: Kveik strains compared for brewers working in Indian heat
title: Kveik Strains Compared for Indian Heat | Craft Beer School
desc: Voss, Hornindal, Lutra and other kveik strains compared on temperature, flavour and speed, for brewers fermenting in hot Indian conditions.
teaser: Voss smells of orange peel, Hornindal of pineapple, Lutra of almost nothing. Picking the right kveik matters as much as the temperature.
standfirst: Kveik yeasts from Norwegian farmhouse brewing ferment cleanly at temperatures that would ruin most ale strains. That makes them attractive in India. But the strains differ a lot. Choosing one for the beer you want is more useful than treating kveik as a single yeast.
sections: What kveik is and why it suits India

Kveik is a Norwegian word for yeast, used for farmhouse cultures handed down in western Norway. Traditional brewers pitched them into warm wort and dried them between brews. Over generations, these cultures became tolerant of heat, fast and reliable.

Most kveik strains ferment well at 30 to 40 °C, often finishing in two to four days, with fewer harsh fusel alcohols than ordinary ale yeast at those temperatures. For a brewery without glycol, or a homebrewer in a Chennai summer, that is a real advantage. Our guide to kveik yeast for hot climates covers the basics.

Voss is probably the most widely used kveik. It is sold as a liquid culture by several yeast labs and as a dry yeast.

Voss gives a clear orange peel and citrus character at higher temperatures, often around 35 to 40 °C. It flocculates well, so beer clears quickly. It works in pale ales, IPAs and blonde ales where citrus helps. At the lower end of its range the orange note becomes quieter.

Hornindal is known for a strong tropical fruit character, often described as pineapple, mango and tangerine. It usually ferments around 30 to 37 °C.

It suits hazy IPAs and fruit-forward pale ales, where the esters work with tropical hops. It can be quite intense, so in a beer meant to be clean, it may be too much. Hornindal is also less flocculent than Voss in many reports, so allow time for clearing or cold crash.

Lutra is a kveik isolate sold as a liquid culture and known for an unusually clean profile. Fermented warm, it can make a crisp, lager-like beer without the long cold fermentation and lagering that true lager needs.

It is not a real lager. Experienced lager drinkers may notice the difference. But for a brewpub in a hot city without much cooling, a Lutra pseudo-lager can be a useful way to offer a clean, crisp beer. Other strains such as Ebbegarden and Stranda have their own fans, with fruit and spice profiles between the clean and the very fruity strains.

• Pale ale or IPA with citrus hops: Voss.
  • Hazy or tropical IPA: Hornindal.
  • Clean, crisp pseudo-lager or blonde: Lutra.
  • Farmhouse or traditional style: a mixed or traditional kveik culture.

Run a small trial before committing a full tank. Split one wort between two strains and taste the results side by side. Keep the temperature, hops and pitch rate the same so the yeast is the only thing that changes. Twenty litres of each is plenty to judge.

Kveik tolerates heat, but it is not magic.

  • Nutrients matter. Fast, hot fermentations need healthy yeast. Add yeast nutrient to the boil, especially in high-adjunct worts. Our guide to yeast nutrition explains why.
  • Pitch rates can be lower. Kveik is often pitched at lower rates than standard ale yeast without problems.
  • Control the top end. Even kveik can produce solvent-like notes if fermentation runs away above its comfortable range. A fermenter that starts at 32 °C can climb several degrees from its own heat.
  • Expect fast finishes. Check gravity daily. A kveik beer may be at final gravity on day three.

One of the pleasures of kveik is how well it reuses. Collect yeast from the bottom of the fermenter or the krausen, store it cold for short periods or dry it in thin layers in a clean, warm place, as traditional brewers did.

Dried kveik keeps for months in a sealed container in the fridge. Label each batch with the strain and date. Mixed cultures can drift over many generations, so restart from a fresh pack if the flavour changes.
Where kveik fits and where it does not

Kveik is excellent for hoppy and fruity beers in hot conditions. It is not a substitute for a true lager yeast and cold fermentation if you want a classic pilsner. It is also not a substitute for a Belgian or German wheat yeast, which bring their own spice and banana.

Used where it fits, kveik solves a real problem for Indian brewers. Our guide to fermenting through an Indian summer covers the other tools.
faqs: Lutra is known for a very clean profile and is often used for crisp, lager-like beers fermented warm.
What temperature should I ferment Voss kveik?
Voss is commonly fermented around 35 to 40 °C, where it gives a clear orange and citrus character.
Can kveik make a real lager?
No. It can make a clean, crisp pseudo-lager, but true lager uses lager yeast fermented cold.
